title: Residual PPO for Body Leveling of Wheel-Legged Robots During Obstacle Traversal
author: Junxian Zhu
affiliation: Mechanical Engineering and Materials Science · Duke University
intro: Recorded motion provides reference joint and wheel commands. Residual Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) uses robot-state feedback to adjust these commands during obstacle traversal, with body leveling evaluated on 50 mm and 100 mm steps.

videos.title: 100 mm · nominal traversal
videos.conditions: 100 mm step · 218.5 mm initial gap · friction multiplier 1.000
videos.watch: Body inclination during wheel unloading, transfer and reloading.
videos.result: Both controllers complete the traversal. The PPO sequence exhibits lower sustained chassis inclination during the central part of the crossing; posture changes remain during subsequent wheel transfers.

videos.title: 50 mm · nominal traversal
videos.conditions: 50 mm step · 218.5 mm initial gap · friction multiplier 1.000
videos.watch: Body posture and wheel contact transitions during the four wheel transfers.
videos.result: Both controllers complete this nominal traversal. The paired views show the chassis attitude and changing wheel contacts throughout the recorded sequence.

videos.title: 100 mm · longer approach distance
videos.conditions: 100 mm step · 238.5 mm initial gap · friction multiplier 1.000
videos.watch: Approach motion and wheel transfers with an increased initial gap.
videos.result: Both controllers complete this condition. The initial gap is 20 mm greater than in the nominal traversal; conditions are matched between the two views within this clip.

videos.title: 100 mm · body-collision termination
videos.conditions: 100 mm step · 207.7 mm initial gap · friction multiplier 1.176
videos.watch: The PPO collision and the subsequent completion of Recorded Replay.
videos.result: The PPO trial terminates with a logged body collision. Recorded Replay completes the same condition. The earlier-ending view holds its final measured pose while the other trial continues.
